reading.body:
Flexential Atlanta - Norcross publishes 1.8 MW of IT capacity across 32,740 square feet of technical space, making it a compliance-oriented colocation site rather than a node for large-scale AI compute.

The power envelope is too small to support significant GPU cluster deployments. At common AI training density of 40 kW per rack, 1.8 MW supports roughly 45 racks. At colocation density of 10 kW per rack, it supports roughly 180 racks. The floor area is large relative to the power figure, which implies either low average rack density or significant white space, though published data does not confirm which.

Six certifications qualify this facility to host regulated workloads in financial services, healthcare, and retail: SOC 1 Type 2 and SOC 2 Type 2 for audited controls, PCI DSS for payment card environments, ISO 27001 for information security management, HITRUST for healthcare data, and SSAE 18 as the underlying attestation standard. Which tenants occupy the facility is not published.

Among 33 facilities mapped in Georgia, only four publish megawatt figures, with combined capacity of 66.3 MW. This campus ranks fourth among those four, contributing 1.8 MW, or roughly 2.7 percent of the state's published total. No expansion plan appears in the data.
